content:
For any desired number \(N\), choose \(N\) target cells whose closed neighborhoods are pairwise disjoint (possible in the infinite triangular grid).

For one such target cell \(c\), shoot repeatedly at \(c\). The possible hit cells are exactly the 4 cells in \(N[c]\). If no cell in \(N[c]\) has been hit 5 times, then all 4 cells have at most 4 hits. To avoid creating a fifth hit, the adversary must choose only cells with at most 3 hits. Each of the 4 cells can be raised to 4 at most once, so after at most \(4\cdot 4=16\) shots all four have 4 hits. On the next shot, one of them must receive its fifth hit.

Thus the shooter can force one cell in \(N[c]\) to be hit exactly 5 times. Since the chosen neighborhoods are disjoint, doing this successively for all \(N\) chosen cells leaves the previously completed cells untouched.

Therefore he can guarantee arbitrarily many cells hit exactly five times; there is no finite maximum.

\[
\boxed{\text{No finite maximum; arbitrarily many}}
\]
